verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā parittaṁ nakhasikhāyaṁ paṁsuṁ āropetvā bhikkhū āmantesi:
verses.english: Then the Buddha, picking up a little bit of dirt on his fingernail, addressed the mendicants:

verses.pali: katamaṁ nu kho bahutaraṁ, yo cāyaṁ mayā paritto nakhasikhāyaṁ paṁsu āropito yā cāyaṁ mahāpathavī”ti?
verses.english: Which is more: the little bit of dirt on my fingernail, or this great earth?”
“Sir, the great earth is far more.

verses.pali: Appamattakoyaṁ bhagavatā paritto nakhasikhāyaṁ paṁsu āropito.
verses.english: The little bit of dirt on your fingernail is tiny.

verses.pali: Saṅkhampi na upeti upanidhimpi na upeti kalabhāgampi na upeti mahāpathaviṁ upanidhāya bhagavatā paritto nakhasikhāyaṁ paṁsu āropito”ti.
verses.english: Compared to the great earth, it doesn’t count, there’s no comparison, it’s not worth a fraction.”

verses.pali: “Evameva kho, bhikkhave, appakā te sattā ye manussesu paccājāyanti;
verses.english: “In the same way the sentient beings reborn as humans are few,

verses.pali: atha kho eteyeva bahutarā sattā ye aññatra manussehi paccājāyanti.
verses.english: while those not reborn as humans are many.
So you should train like this:
